textData.text: Voyage 001 · 16 November 2026 · Full edition · 16 pages · 88 sources, each read and checked
Suez reopens. Hormuz doesn't. Your freight bill sits in between.

Container lines are coming back through the canal and spot rates are easing. The Gulf war keeps fuel, air cargo and Gulf-bound freight expensive. Sixteen pages on what both mean for cargo that touches Egypt.

Evergreen and ONE sent ships through the Suez Canal this month for the first time in nearly three years, and the canal earned $724m in October, its best month since the Red Sea crisis began. In the Strait of Hormuz, traffic is still about 65% below pre-war levels, and at least 10 ships were hit in the first ten days of November.
Evergreen back 8 Nov, ONE 15 Nov; October transits +32% to 1.5k, revenue $724m (+94%).
Red Sea · Bab al-Mandab: Half capacity.
467,297 TEU/week committed in October, 50% of pre-crisis; IMO still condemns Houthi attacks.
Traffic ~65% below pre-war; 181 incidents logged since 1 March (JMIC).
Cape of Good Hope: Still in use.
Most Asia–North Europe loops still route via the Cape (Hapag-Lloyd).
34 daily slots and the 50ft Neopanamax draft restored (9 Nov advisory).
This is the full edition of
, the weekly review we publish every Monday for exporters, importers, manufacturers and fellow forwarders who move cargo through Egypt.
Every figure is footnoted to the page we read it on. Where we could not verify a claim, we left it out; where a claim comes from one side of a conflict, we say so. The analysis lines marked
are ours, and they are kept apart from the reporting. —

Rockit's read: Three moves for this week
Book December cargo against index-linked or negotiated rates, not the $6,500–6,600 tariff, and ask for an all-in quote that lists every surcharge.
Check whether your markets are on the 50% freight-support list, and build complete rebate files from the first shipment: incomplete files are now refused.
Shipping to the Gulf or by air?
Confirm the routing (Gulf bypass ports or Saudi Red Sea ports) and lock air space before the late-November peak.

The index says down. The tariff says up.
Three independent indices put Asia–Med spot between $4,168 and $4,666 a box. December's published tariffs to Egypt start at $6,500.

Spot container rates eased again last week. Drewry's World Container Index fell 2% to $4,305 per 40ft on 12 November. Shanghai–Rotterdam slipped 3% to $3,504, while Shanghai–Genoa, Drewry's closest proxy for Egypt's Mediterranean ports, held at $4,168. Freightos put Asia–Mediterranean at $4,300 (−1%), and Xeneta's Far East–Med average was $4,666 (−0.9%) on 13 November.

Carriers are pricing December differently. Hapag-Lloyd's Far East–Europe tariff from 1 December sets Türkiye, Egypt and the Eastern Mediterranean at $5,300 per 20ft and $6,600 per 40ft. MSC's December rate lifts East Med 40ft boxes by $800 to $6,500, valid to 14 December at the latest. From 15 November MSC also adds a combined $91 per TEU piracy-risk and Suez Canal surcharge on Asian cargo to the remaining Mediterranean, North African and Black Sea ports.

Drewry counts eight blank sailings on Asia–Europe/Med next week, up from five, and still expects those rates to “increase slightly in the coming weeks”. Xeneta's chief analyst Peter Sand is less convinced: “gravity always wins”.

A published tariff is a carrier's opening position, not the market. With the gap at roughly $1,800–2,400 per 40ft, Asia–Egypt importers have room to negotiate below December's tariffs, but only with an all-in quote that names every surcharge.

The canal's comeback, service by service
Every major alliance now has at least one service through Suez again. Most North Europe loops are still on the Cape.
transited northbound on 8 November, the carrier's first Suez passage since it suspended Red Sea routings in December 2023. A week later, on 15 November, ONE's 8,110 TEU

crossed southbound on the Premier Alliance FE1 loop. Suez Canal Authority chairman Ossama Rabiee said three more Premier Alliance services will switch from the Cape to the canal; Freightos expects Yang Ming in December and full alliance returns by Q1 2027.

Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd moved their joint ME1 India–Europe service to Suez in early November. Hapag-Lloyd now routes five Far East–South Europe services, one Far East–North Europe service and two India–Europe services through the canal; its other North Europe services still sail via the Cape.

The money is following. Canal revenue reached $724m in October, up 94% year on year and the highest since the Red Sea crisis began, on transits up 32% to 1.5k. Xeneta counts 467,297 TEU of weekly capacity committed to the Red Sea in October: half the pre-crisis level, and roughly double the end-of-August figure.
The services recovering first are the ones that pass Egypt: Asia–South Europe and India–Europe. Check each booking's routing (Suez or Cape) rather than assume it.

Flexport, quoted by The Loadstar, warns that ships arriving via Suez and the Cape together could push North Europe arriving capacity to 131% of normal in week 47.

UKMTO's latest weekly count, reported on 13 November, was 139 outbound and 169 inbound Hormuz transits, with traffic about 65% below pre-conflict levels and eight incidents, seven of them tanker attacks. The Joint Maritime Information Center has logged 181 incidents since 1 March and about 211 ships waiting at anchor east of the strait.

Suez routings burn less fuel than the Cape. Fuel recovery charges should follow, slowly.

Xeneta forecasts global spot rates 30% lower in 2027 and long-term rates 5% lower, against Q3 2026. It expects fleet growth of 6.8% against demand growth of 2.5–4%, and says the Suez return has already released 599k TEU of capacity.
Avoid locking Q4 2026 price levels into long 2027 contracts. Shorter or index-linked terms keep the upside.
Panama: 34 slots a day, 50ft draft restored
The Panama Canal Authority raised daily transit capacity from 33 to 34 slots and restored the 15.24m (50ft) Neopanamax draft, citing improved lake levels.
US West Coast: Watchmen strike deadline moves to 20 November
Talks between the PMA and ILWU Local 26 now run to 20 November; Local 26 works terminals handling about 85% of Long Beach cargo. Los Angeles handled a record 1,026,872 TEU in October.

Rockit explains · in one paragraph: Why spot and tariff diverge in a reopening

When ships return to a shorter route, the same fleet can make more voyages, so effective capacity rises before demand does. Spot rates, set by cargo chasing space week by week, react first. Tariffs and surcharges, set by carriers trying to protect revenue, react last. Xeneta estimates the Suez return has already released 599k TEU of capacity and forecasts spot rates 30% lower in 2027. The gap between index and tariff is the negotiating room.
A peak season priced like one
Rates are at their 2026 high, fuel has doubled, and Gulf capacity is still 18% short of pre-war.

The Baltic Air Freight Index rose 5.3% in the four weeks to 2 November, leaving it 22.8% above last year and above the highest points of the previous two peak seasons, TAC Index says. In the week to 9 November it rose another 6.6% to its highest level of 2026, with “chunky gains” from Europe on routes including to the UAE.

IATA's September data show demand (CTK) up 7.7% against capacity up 2.7%, lifting the global load factor to 47.9%. Middle Eastern carriers had the weakest demand growth, +3.8%, while adding 7.0% capacity; Europe–Middle East traffic fell 18.0%. Jet fuel was 103.4% above a year earlier.

WorldACD's October figures put Africa-origin spot rates at $3.11/kg, up 60% year on year, as tight capacity and fuel surcharges met the start of the perishables export season. Capacity to and from Arabian Gulf markets was still 18% below its pre-war level. Xeneta sees few signs of a further Christmas surge and expects some cargo to shift back to ocean from Q2 2027.

Egyptian perishables and urgent-parts shippers should book capacity now and budget for fuel surcharges well above last year. Express heavyweight services are a fallback when general cargo space runs out.

Rockit's read: What the forwarder results mean for you

The big forwarders are earning more from air freight by choosing which cargo to carry: tech and hyperscaler freight gets space first, and DSV says it is trading volume for yield. Smaller shippers should hold block-space or allocation agreements, or work through a forwarder that does. Consolidation among mid-tier forwarders also means agency networks will change; check who your partner's partner is.

E-commerce: Europe's de minimis ends, parcels drop

Since the EU's €3 duty on parcels under €150 began on 1 July, Asia–Europe e-commerce air volumes fell 61% year on year in Q3 (Xeneta). WorldACD reports a further €2-per-item EU handling fee from 1 November, expected to cut volumes further.

Denmark's Scan Global Logistics agreed to buy OIA Global (1,200 staff, 30+ countries), aiming for the global top 20; closing is expected in Q1 2027. AIT Worldwide completed its purchase of Australia's Connor Anderson.
Technology: Quotes in minutes, B/Ls on screen

CH Robinson says AI agents cut air quotes from a day, and ocean quotes from two to three days, to two to three minutes. DCSA reports Korea's eBL platform completed full-lifecycle tests with HMM, with live shipments targeted within 2026.
Sustainability: DHL Express flies SAF out of Paris, including to Casablanca

DHL Express signed a one-year deal with TotalEnergies for 5m litres of sustainable aviation fuel on flights from Paris CDG to Leipzig, Casablanca, Milan and London, cutting about 11,800t of CO₂e a year. SAF was 10% of fuel on DHL's own fleet in 2025.
European buyers that report Scope 3 emissions may start asking Egyptian exporters for lower-carbon transport options.
Carriers in logistics: Maersk's logistics arm outgrows its ships
Maersk's Logistics & Services revenue rose 13% in Q3 and its EBIT margin improved to 5.8%, while ocean volumes slipped about 1%, FreightWaves reports.
People: DHL names a Sub-Saharan Africa forwarding chief
DHL Global Forwarding appointed Sascha Geiken CEO for Sub-Saharan Africa (excluding South Africa) on 10 November.
Every deadline now lands on 9 January
Both sides of the US–China truce, and the US port fees on Chinese ships, expire within a day of each other.

The US Trade Representative suspended its Section 301 port fees on Chinese-built and Chinese-operated ships for two more months, to 11:59pm ET on 9 January 2027 (91 FR 72608, published 10 November). The same day it extended all 178 remaining product exclusions in the main Section 301 China tariff case to the same date.

China mirrored the move. Its 24% additional tariff on US goods stays suspended for two more months (a 10% tariff remains), and its port fees on US-linked ships and critical-mineral export waivers run to 10 January. Reuters reported that Xi and Trump were expected to meet at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18–19 November.

The tariffs struck down in February stay in the news. After the Supreme Court ruled the IEEPA tariffs unlawful, UPS has gone to the Court of International Trade to force refunds on finally liquidated entries; The Loadstar reports UPS has received about $500m and still owes customers $270m. China's commerce ministry noted that Washington intends to use Section 301 tariffs to replace the IEEPA duties. On Section 232, the White House chose 180 days of talks rather than tariffs on robotics and industrial machinery.
US-lane quotes that run past 9 January need a surcharge clause. Egyptian exporters who shipped DDP to the US should check who was importer of record: refund rights follow that name.

Energy: Diesel at $180, Iran's exports near zero

The IEA says Gulf oil exports excluding Oman were 18.4m barrels a day in October, 26% below pre-war. European diesel is near $180 a barrel, about 77% above pre-war. Iranian crude exports have dwindled to almost nothing under the US naval blockade, and FGE's Fereidun Fesharaki says “we are not close to a resolution”.

War at sea: IMO: 133 incidents, 25 seafarers killed

The IMO Council (2–6 Nov) condemned Houthi attacks in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab and Russian attacks on Ukraine's Black Sea corridor. The IMO counts 133 confirmed incidents and 25 seafarer deaths since the conflict began on 28 February; on 11 November its Secretary-General urged strict SOLAS enforcement in Hormuz.
Keep war-risk and deviation clauses in Red Sea contracts even as carriers return.
Black Sea: Russia claims hits on three cargo ships

Russia's defence ministry said overnight strikes, reported on 8 November, hit a container ship at Odesa, another at Chornomorsk and a dry-cargo ship south-west of Odesa. Reuters could not verify the claims, and Ukraine did not immediately comment.
Egypt buys Black Sea wheat; insurance and freight on that corridor stay high.
Sanctions: US and EU rules on Russia diverge
, carrying about 40,000t of Russian diesel under last month's Putin–Trump supply deal, made a U-turn about 400nm off New York. Bloomberg tracking shows no Russian diesel cargo has yet reached the US.
Screen Russia-linked cargo and tonnage against US, EU and UK lists separately.

The IMO set MEPC 85 for 30 Nov–3 Dec. gCaptain reported in September that the framework could return for adoption at an extraordinary session on 4 December. If adopted, it enters into force 16 months later for ships over 5,000 GT.
Carbon · EU: CBAM certificates get pricier

The Commission's CBAM certificate price rose to €82.32 for Q3, from €75.28 in Q2. Certificates will be bought on a central platform from February 2027, and the first declarations are due by 30 September 2027. Importers of more than 50t of CBAM goods need declarant status.
Carbon · shipping: EU ETS now bills 100%
Shipping lines surrendered allowances for 70% of verified 2025 emissions on 30 September. For 2026 emissions the share is 100%, and methane and nitrous oxide are now included.
Check ETS surcharges on Egypt–EU legs in 2027 tariffs.
Cairo will pay half the freight, if the file is complete
A revamped rebate programme gives freight its own support line, and refuses incomplete files.

The Cabinet approved the revamped export rebate programme on 5 November. Support rises by an average of 35%, and the new rates already apply to shipments from the start of November; free-zone exporters are excluded. For the first time, freight has its own line: the state covers 50% of sea and land freight to Africa, Latin America, Australia, Southeast Asia and Russia, and for agricultural exports 25% of air freight to Europe and 50% to the UK.

The programme also pays 25% of domestic transport, of cargo insurance and of express-vessel invoices. The US and 11 Southeast Asian countries join the target-market list. Exporters must submit complete files before they are accepted. Phase one runs to the end of 2026 and phase two starts in July 2027. The FY 2026/27 budget earmarks EGP 48bn for export support, against EGP 28bn actually paid out last year.
Freight invoices, B/Ls and insurance certificates are now part of the exporter's cash flow. Ask your forwarder for claim-ready documents from the first shipment.

FX outlook: Banks split on the pound

Deutsche Bank sees the pound at 48 per dollar if the US–Iran war ends and beyond 60 if it escalates, and expects the CBE to hold rates. It says it has not heard of “significant import delays” from FX shortages. Remittances hit a record $38.2bn in January–September.
Freight is billed in dollars. Watch quote validity and FX clauses.

Gas cuts for fertiliser and methanol plants rose to 33%, and Ezz Steel was notified of a 30% cut, per Asharq Business (disputed by an industry source). Five of 15 November LNG cargoes were deferred, and urea is fetching about $535/t.
Expect lumpier urea, ammonia and methanol export volumes; confirm cargo readiness.
SCZone: Sokhna gets a digital truck yard

SCZone hired Telecom Egypt to upgrade networks at East Port Said and Sokhna. A Nafeza-run digital truck yard at Sokhna will handle up to 1.1k trucks a day, and Sailun's $804m tyre plant rolled out its first tyre.
EU: CBAM bill: about $317m a year

Egypt is asking Brussels for a phased CBAM timetable. Environment Ministry studies put the cost of non-compliance at about $317m a year, of which steel accounts for $236m. Separately, the EU plans to recognise Egyptian e-signatures, a first outside Europe.

DP World has moved more than 1m TEU overland from UAE east-coast ports since March, about 3.5k TEU a day. AD Ports posted record Q3 net income of AED 975m, while UAE container throughput fell 57%. GCC states signed the framework for a 2.1k-km railway.
Quote Gulf cargo via Khorfakkan, Fujairah or Sohar plus trucking, or via Saudi Red Sea ports.
State finances: A gate on public FX spending
The Cabinet approved three months of spending rationalisation: any state spending with a foreign-currency component now needs Finance Ministry approval, coordinated with the CBE.
Rail: Sinai freight line gathers pace
Egypt is accelerating construction of a 341km railway linking Bir al-Abd, Arish and Taba, Daily News Egypt reports.
Energy routes: Iraqi crude looks for Red Sea and Med outlets

Iraqi, Egyptian and Jordanian officials discussed new Red Sea and Mediterranean outlets for Iraqi crude, including the $4.6bn Basra–Haditha pipeline (about 2.3m barrels a day). No terminals or timetable were named.
United States: Cairo takes US trade barriers to the USTR
Investment and Foreign Trade Minister Mohamed Farid met US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer in Washington to review the economic partnership and discuss bilateral trade flows.

Sudan lifted its import ban on 44 of 46 goods and zeroed duties on staples. The PM proposed extending the Alexandria–Koper port partnership to Sokhna and Damietta. DP World starts a weekly China–East Africa link in late November.
Rockit explains: Anatomy of an Asia → Egypt ocean quote
Spot indices, published tariffs and the number on your invoice are three different things. In December they are far apart, so it pays to know which line is which.
FAK tariff, or a negotiated / index-linked rate
Ask: Is this tariff, spot or contract? Which index is it linked to?
BAF or MFR: bunker cost recovery
Ask: Is fuel included in the base? Which month's fuel price?
Peak season (PSS), piracy-risk, Suez Canal, security, EU ETS on EU legs
Ask: List every surcharge and its effective date
Suez or Cape of Good Hope
Ask: Which way does this service sail? Transit days?
THC, documentation, free time at Alexandria, Damietta, Port Said or Sokhna
Ask: Free days for demurrage and detention?
The date the price stops holding (MSC's December FAK: 14 Dec at the latest)
Ask: Valid until which date: booking, loading or sailing?

Freight All Kinds: a carrier's published base rate for general cargo, regardless of commodity.
General Rate Increase: an announced across-the-board rate rise; not always achieved in the market.
Peak Season Surcharge: an add-on charged in busy periods.
Bunker Adjustment Factor / Marine Fuel Recovery: the fuel component of a sea freight rate.
Twenty- and forty-foot equivalent units: one 40ft box is two TEU.
Drewry World Container Index and Freightos Baltic Index: weekly spot-rate benchmarks.
Cargo tonne-kilometres (demand) and available cargo tonne-kilometres (capacity) in air freight.
Baltic Air Freight Index, global: TAC Index's air rate benchmark.
A scheduled voyage a carrier cancels to cut capacity.
The value below which parcels enter a country duty-free; the EU removed it on 1 July 2026.
US trade law used for tariffs and port fees on China.
